Represent all hierarchical series as $y=Sb$, where $b$ contains bottom-level series and $S$ aggregates them. Bottom-up forecasts the leaves and sums them; top-down allocates an aggregate forecast using proportions. Both are coherent but can discard useful signals at other levels. MinT reconciles arbitrary base forecasts using their error covariance $W$. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

$$\tilde y=S(S^TW^{-1}S)^{-1}S^TW^{-1}\hat y.$$

The reconciled vector lies in the column space of $S$, so store totals equal regions and national totals. Estimate horizon-specific forecast-error covariance with shrinkage when history is limited; noisy covariance estimates can undermine the theoretical gain. Standard linear reconciliation does not guarantee nonnegative forecasts or coherent prediction intervals. Use constrained or probabilistic reconciliation if those properties are required, and evaluate every hierarchy level.
